fields.requires: prérequis strict : on ne peut pas maîtriser le point sans eux (utilisé pour déduire dans le test de placement)
fields.after: ordre conseillé du parcours seulement (jamais utilisé pour déduire)
fields.detect: précision mesurée du repérage dans les livres (null : pas encore mesurée ; surlignage à partir de 0,9)

points.title: Le verbe to be au présent
points.example: She is tired. They aren't here.

points.title: Prétérit de be : was / were
points.example: I was at home. Were you tired?

points.title: Pronoms sujets et compléments
points.example: She likes him. They called us.

points.title: Adjectifs et pronoms possessifs
points.example: my, your, his, her, its, their ; mine, yours

points.title: Articles a / an / the
points.example: a book, an apple, the sun

points.title: Formes du pluriel
points.example: boxes, cities, children, men

points.title: Démonstratifs this / that / these / those
points.example: These shoes are new.

points.title: Adjectif : place et invariabilité
points.example: a red car, different ideas

points.title: Présent simple
points.example: He works in London.
points.falsePositive: formes identiques au prétérit ou à l'infinitif (put, cut)

points.title: Questions et négations avec do / does
points.example: Does she speak French? I don't know.

points.title: Questions avec mot interrogatif
points.example: Where do you live? What did she say?

points.title: There is / there are
points.example: There are two cafés near here.

points.title: Have / have got (possession)
points.example: I've got a brother. Do you have a car?
points.falsePositive: have got = present perfect de get

points.title: Can / can't (capacité, permission)
points.example: Can you swim? I can't come.

points.title: L'impératif
points.example: Sit down. Don't worry.

points.title: Prépositions de temps et de lieu : in / on / at
points.example: at 6 pm, on Monday, in July
points.falsePositive: chaque in / on / at : surligner n'apprend rien

points.title: Adverbes de fréquence et leur place
points.example: I always get up early. She is never late.

points.title: Présent continu (be + -ing)
points.example: She's reading right now.

points.title: Présent simple ou continu
points.example: I usually walk, but today I'm driving.

points.title: Prétérit des verbes réguliers
points.example: We watched a film yesterday.

points.title: Prétérit des verbes irréguliers
points.example: She went home and wrote a letter.

points.title: Participe passé (réguliers et irréguliers)
points.example: gone, written, taken, watched

points.title: Questions et négations au prétérit (did)
points.example: Did you see it? I didn't go.

points.title: Prétérit continu (was / were + -ing)
points.example: I was cooking when he called.

points.title: Noms indénombrables
points.example: some advice, much information, furniture

points.title: Some / any, much / many, a lot of
points.example: How much money? How many people?

points.title: Comparatifs et superlatifs
points.example: bigger, more expensive, the best

points.title: Le génitif 's et of
points.example: my sister's room, the end of the film

points.title: Futur avec be going to
points.example: It's going to rain.
points.falsePositive: going to + lieu (I'm going to Paris)

points.title: Futur avec will (décision, prédiction)
points.example: I'll call you later.

points.title: Obligation : must / have to
points.example: You must stop. I have to work.

points.title: Conseil : should
points.example: You should rest.

points.title: Adverbes de manière (-ly) et leur place
points.example: She drives carefully. I speak English well.

points.title: Verbe + -ing ou verbe + to
points.example: I enjoy cooking. I want you to come.

points.title: Present perfect (expérience, résultat)
points.example: Have you ever been to Rome? I've lost my keys.

points.title: Present perfect ou prétérit
points.example: I saw him yesterday. I've seen him today.

points.title: For / since (durée jusqu'à maintenant)
points.example: I've lived here since 2019 / for five years.

points.title: Present perfect continu
points.example: She's been waiting for an hour.

points.title: Plus-que-parfait (had + participe)
points.example: When I arrived, the film had started.

points.title: Used to (habitudes passées)
points.example: I used to smoke.
points.falsePositive: be used to (passif de use : it was used to open)

points.title: Conditionnel réel (if + présent, will)
points.example: If it rains, we'll stay home.

points.title: When / as soon as / until + présent
points.example: Call me when you arrive.

points.title: Conditionnel irréel (if + prétérit, would)
points.example: If I had time, I would travel.

points.title: Passif au présent et au prétérit
points.example: The bridge was built in 1890.

points.title: Relatives déterminatives (who / which / that, relatif omis)
points.example: The man (who) I met was French.

points.title: Déduction au présent : must / might / can't
points.example: She must be tired. It can't be true.

points.title: Discours rapporté (affirmations)
points.example: He said (that) he was tired.

points.title: Few / little / a few / a little, every / each
points.example: I have a few friends but little time.

points.title: Say ou tell
points.example: She told me the truth. He said hello.

points.title: Stop / remember / try + -ing ou + to (changement de sens)
points.example: I stopped smoking. I stopped to smoke.

points.title: Questions sur le sujet (sans do)
points.example: Who called you? What happened?

points.title: Le but : to + base verbale
points.example: I came to learn English.

points.title: Préposition + -ing
points.example: before leaving, I look forward to seeing you

points.title: Questions indirectes
points.example: Can you tell me where the station is?

points.title: Too / enough / so / such
points.example: too expensive, old enough, so kind, such a nice day

points.title: Make / let + base verbale
points.example: She made me wait. Let me go.

points.title: Verbes à particule : place du complément
points.example: Pick it up. Turn the light off.

points.title: Question tags, so do I / neither do I
points.example: It's cold, isn't it? So do I.

points.title: Conditionnel passé (if + had + participe)
points.example: If I had known, I would have come.

points.title: Conditionnels mixtes
points.example: If I had studied, I would be a doctor now.

points.title: Wish / if only (regrets, souhaits)
points.example: I wish I knew. If only I had listened.

points.title: Passif avec un modal
points.example: It must be done. It can't be fixed.

points.title: Have something done
points.example: I had my hair cut.

points.title: Relatives explicatives (virgules, which, whose)
points.example: My brother, who lives in Paris, is a chef.

points.title: Déduction au passé : must have / might have / can't have
points.example: He must have missed the train.

points.title: Discours rapporté : questions et ordres
points.example: She asked where I lived. He told me to wait.

points.title: Futur continu
points.example: This time tomorrow I'll be flying.

points.title: Futur antérieur
points.example: I'll have finished by six.

points.title: Be / get used to + -ing
points.example: I'm used to getting up early.

points.title: Inversion après une négation (Never have I…)
points.example: Rarely do we see such talent.

points.title: Phrases clivées (What I need is…, It was… that…)
points.example: What I need is a holiday.

points.title: Propositions participiales
points.example: Having finished, she left. Built in 1890, the house…

points.title: Subjonctif formel (suggest that he go)
points.example: I suggest that he be told.

points.title: Do d'insistance
points.example: I do like it. She did call.

traps.title: Faim, froid, raison… avec be
traps.wrong: I have cold. You have right.

traps.title: Le possessif s'accorde avec le possesseur
Can n'a ni do, ni to, ni futur
traps.wrong: Do you can? I will can.
traps.right: Can you? I will be able to.

traps.title: L'adverbe de fréquence avant le verbe
traps.wrong: I go always to work by bus.
traps.right: I always go to work by bus.

traps.title: Pas de pluriel pour advice, information…
Rien entre le verbe et son complément
Mustn't (interdit) ≠ don't have to (pas obligé)
traps.wrong: You mustn't come if you're busy.
traps.right: You don't have to come if you're busy.

traps.title: The best in, pas of
traps.wrong: the best restaurant of the world
traps.right: the best restaurant in the world

traps.title: Suggest sans to
traps.right: I suggest (that) you go. I suggest going.

traps.title: Pas de the pour une généralité
traps.wrong: The life is short. I love the music.
traps.right: Life is short. I love music.

traps.title: Pas de will après if
traps.wrong: If it will rain, we stay home.
traps.right: If it rains, we'll stay home.

traps.title: Pas de will après when
traps.wrong: When I will arrive, I'll call you.
traps.right: When I arrive, I'll call you.

traps.title: Question sur le sujet sans did
Après une préposition : -ing
traps.wrong: before to leave ; I look forward to see you
traps.right: before leaving ; I look forward to seeing you

traps.title: Pas d'inversion dans une question indirecte
traps.wrong: Can you tell me where is the station?
traps.right: Can you tell me where the station is?

traps.title: Pronom entre le verbe et la particule
Be used to + -ing
traps.wrong: I'm used to get up early.
traps.right: I'm used to getting up early.

traps.title: Pas d'inversion dans une question rapportée
traps.wrong: She asked where did I live.

collections.title: Make ou do (make a mistake, do homework…)
collections.note: Liste de collocations, pas une règle : collection de notes à importer, révisée par FSRS.

collections.title: Verbes et adjectifs à préposition (depend on, listen to, wait for, good at…)
